newsitem.title: POLAND: EIB TO ISSUE 4-5 YEAR POLISH BONDS IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: EIB TO ISSUE 4-5 YEAR POLISH BONDS IN 1997.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) plans to issue four-to-five year zloty-denominated bonds in Poland this year, most likely worth more than 100 million Ecus, EIB's deputy president Wolfgang Roth said on Monday.
"We want to raise funds in zlotys...to provide them for our clients who want to avoid exchange-rate risk," Roth told a news conference in Warsaw.
"In Hungary, we are implementing a programme of bonds worth 100 million Ecus...and I think in Poland the amount could be a bit higher," he added.
Roth said the EIB, the European Union's investment bank, wanted to test the Polish capital market to see if it could become a long-term source of capital.
"We want to test the zloty market...our issue is also a contribution to its development," he said.

Roth said the issue, with maturity of four to five years, was supported by Finance Minister Marek Belka and the central bank because by funding projects with locally borrowed funds the EIB prevented affecting Poland's money supply.
"The zloty bonds will not put pressure on the money supply... and will help their (the finance ministry and central bank) monetary stabilisation policy," he said.
